X.note: Strong, convincing ruined street with raking light and a haze that gives depth. A sparse group of figures sits in the lane. Several are flat, mannequin-like and silhouetted, one is half-naked or dark-skinned with an odd belt, and there are mismatched uniforms. The foreground barrels and rubble help. The figures are too small and dim, so the frame is still a CGI game-engine look rather than broadcast quality.

Y.note: Same set as X, but the crowd of identical red and blue coated soldiers is packed into a block. Their lit faces and bodies look like cloned game assets or paper cut-outs, and they are bright against the dark lane. The blue-coated figures with white crossbelts are odd for a British garrison. The marching ranks block the view down the lane and hide the harbor and the haze. The uniform lighting on the figures does not match the street's raking sun.

why: X keeps the lane's depth, atmosphere and light, with fewer, more varied figures, while Y's cloned, toy-like crowd clutters the vanishing point and looks like game assets.
top_fix_for_weaker: Cut the crowd to a handful of varied figures and give each a distinct pose, uniform and gear. Light and shade them with the street's raking sun and cast shadows. Add haze and ground contact so they sit in the scene, and keep the center of the lane clear.
anachronisms_seen: Blue-coated soldiers with white crossbelts in a British garrison (Hanoverian and Royal Artillery blue is plausible, but the mass of them looks off)
Near-identical uniforms and tricorn hats, looking like cloned assets
Shirtless or dark-skinned figure with a belt in X
Union Jack in the 1801 design (with St Patrick's cross) would be wrong for 1782, and at this resolution it is hard to tell which design it is
Unusually clean, modern-looking shutters and flat building textures
